subject: PlaneGeometry
question:
A spiral of isosceles triangles is constructed counterclockwise, starting with the shaded triangle $B A C$, whose top angle is $\angle B A C=100^{\circ}$. Triangle $\triangle A B C$ is numbered 0. Each subsequent triangle (numbered 1, 2, $3, \ldots$ ) shares exactly one edge with the previous triangle, as shown. What is the number of the first triangle that precisely covers triangle $\mathrm{nr}$. 0?

original_question:
We are going to make a spiral of isosceles triangles. We'll start with the shaded triangle $B A C$, which has a top angle $\angle B A C=100^{\circ}$, and move counterclockwise. Let $\triangle A B C$ have number 0. Every of the next triangles (with numbers 1, 2, $3, \ldots$ ) will have exactly one edge adjoining the previous one (see the picture). What will be the number of the first triangle which precisely covers triangle $\mathrm{nr}$. 0?
